Trade Tech Solutions Adds Perpetuals to Its Prop Firm Technology Following Prediction Markets Launch
summary:
The two launches bring six markets onto one infrastructure used by 85+ prop firms serving more than 2 million users.
Trade Tech Solutions has expanded its prop firm technology to cover perpetuals, following the launch of its prediction markets trading infrastructure in May. The perpetuals offering, which went live in October, lets operators launch a perpetuals prop firm in as little as 25 days. Firms already using Trade Tech Solutions for CFDs, futures, crypto or sports can now add either market through their existing provider.
The new markets run on infrastructure already operating at scale. Trade Tech Solutions powers 85+ prop firms across 180+ regions, including many of the top 15 in CFDs and futures. Firms on its infrastructure serve more than 2 million users and over 1 million active accounts every month, process more than $200 million in client revenues each year and have handled over $100 million in trader payouts to date.
Perpetuals bring round-the-clock risk management
For a prop firm offering perpetuals, risk management runs around the clock. Operators need to track how leverage and funding affect a trader’s position and when liquidation rules apply. Trade Tech Solutions’ perpetuals prop firm technology integrates with Hyperliquid and has those rules built in, with real-time risk management operating 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
The launch package also includes a white-label CRM and a trader dashboard available on the web, iOS and Android. Operators can manage the programme under their own brand, from a trader’s initial evaluation through to funded status. All evaluation and funded accounts are simulated.
Dedicated evaluation rules for prediction markets trading
Prediction markets trading gives prop firms a different way to assess traders who take positions on the outcomes of events. Live since May, Trade Tech Solutions’ prediction markets prop firm technology pairs evaluation rules specific to this market with real-time risk management. An operator running a CFD or futures programme can introduce a separate prediction markets trading challenge while keeping both programmes on the same infrastructure.
Launches in markets other than perpetuals, including prediction markets, can take as little as seven days. Across the infrastructure, payouts are semi-automated and require manual approval.
“Our clients don’t want a different provider for every market they enter,” said Henri, Partnership Manager at Trade Tech Solutions. “With perpetuals now live alongside prediction markets, CFD, futures, crypto and sports, operators can launch a new vertical or move their entire business onto one infrastructure, and established firms can migrate in as little as 48 hours.”
A weekend migration for established firms
For an established firm switching providers, one practical question is what happens to traders partway through a challenge. Trade Tech Solutions’ prop firm migration service carries each trader’s account, challenge progress and funded status across to the new system, together with trading history, payout records and the firm’s risk configurations.
A firm can complete the move over a single weekend. Operators can also move individual components, such as their CRM or risk engine, if they need to replace only part of their setup.
Prop firms and brokers planning a launch or migration can book a call with the Trade Tech Solutions team.

Adyen Partners With OVO to Power Card Payments Across Its Customer Base
summary:
Adyen, the global financial technology platform of choice for leading businesses, is partnering with OVO, one of the UK's largest energy suppliers, to process all of its consumer card payments. The partnership provides OVO with a flexible, robust payments infrastructure designed to support complex utility journeys across its residential base. 
As a leading residential energy supplier accounting for a significant portion of the UK's electricity and gas supply, OVO required a payments solution capable of handling a diverse customer base with differing financial circumstances. By leveraging Adyen's strong APIs and comprehensive payment capabilities, OVO can now offer highly flexible payment options, including advanced billing and scheduling functionality. This ensures a simple, reliable experience whether customers are making one-off top-ups, weekly payments, or managing complex recurring utility schedules. 
“We are constantly finding ways to support our customers and make managing home energy as simple and transparent as possible,” said Fiona Taylor, Strategy Lead, Payments at OVO. “Our partnership with Adyen will bring next-generation flexibility to payment schedules, ensuring that whether a customer is topping up, paying weekly, or managing a complex cycle, their experience is simple, reliable, and built around their needs.” 
“Energy is an essential utility, yet the payment experience has historically been rigid and unforgiving,” said Nicole Olbe, President for EMEA at Adyen. “OVO is changing that by putting the customer's financial reality first. We are incredibly proud to provide the technological backbone for this shift, delivering a payments experience that offers real flexibility to over three and a half million households.” 
The successful go-live of consumer card payments marks the beginning of a strategic collaboration between Adyen and OVO. As the energy provider continues to innovate its digital services, this robust, secure payments foundation will support ongoing enhancements to the customer experience across the UK energy market.

RingGo Announces American Express Payment Option for Majority of Parking Locations Across the UK
summary:
RingGo by Arrive, the UK’s number one mobile parking app, has started to roll out the option for drivers to pay for parking using American Express credit cards. The announcement is an expansion of the number of payment methods available, responding to customer demand, and can be used in the RingGo by Arrive app, over the phone. 
To date motorists have been able to pay using other credit or debit cards as well as mobile wallets like Google Pay and Apple Pay. RingGo by Arrive is beginning to roll out American Express as a payment option with partners across the country. Today RingGo users in the majority of towns, cities and boroughs will be able to start paying with American Express. The roll out will continue throughout the rest of the year. 
 

Adam Dolphin, Regional Director for the UK & Ireland at Arrive, says: “Our goal is to make payment as easy as possible for as many of our users as possible. Adding American Express to our credit card payment options is something our customers have requested and we are pleased to be able to now offer it.”
Motorists who use RingGo have various ways to pay. The most popular choice is via the app – which can be downloaded free of charge from the App Store or Google Play – or they can call, text or visit RingGo.co.uk. 
Those who have not used RingGo before must register to use the service by downloading the free RingGo app and inputting details, or visiting RingGo.co.uk and completing the registration. Existing RingGo users can simply add the relevant location code, start a session and park in a couple of taps.

PayPoint and Engage Hub Deepen Payment Partnership for Housing Associations
summary:
Engage Hub, the data-driven AI journey automation company, and PayPoint, digital payments expert, today announced the expansion of their partnership to provide housing associations with PCI-compliant payment journeys that protect sensitive customer data while improving the resident experience.
Thirteen housing associations currently use the solution, which lets residents make secure payments over the phone while remaining connected to a customer service adviser. This improves accessibility and protects people who need additional assistance.
Delivering seamless and secure payments
The solution combines Engage Hub’s customer journey orchestration and PCI-compliant payment capabilities with PayPoint’s established payment infrastructure, which features tone masking technology to prevent agents accessing residents’ card information. It can be deployed within existing contact centre environments, easily integrates with a broad range of CRM software, and works across hybrid and remote contact centre operations.
“Organisations are increasingly looking for payment experiences that combine robust security with ease of use and accessibility,” said Simon Coles, Digital Payments and Open Banking Managing Director at PayPoint. “Our continued partnership with Engage Hub helps housing associations modernise payment journeys, reduce compliance complexity and deliver better outcomes for both residents and customer service teams.”
Enabling connected customer experiences across voice and digital channels
“It’s fantastic to see growing adoption as organisations look to modernise resident engagement while maintaining the highest security levels,” said Simon Brennan, VP Sales Europe at Engage Hub. “Together with PayPoint, we’re helping housing associations simplify compliance, improve operational efficiency and deliver more connected journeys across the various channels residents use.”
The expanded partnership builds on Engage Hub and PayPoint’s successful 4-year collaboration. It forms part of Engage Hub’s broader strategy to help organisations orchestrate secure, intelligent and customer-centric journeys across voice, messaging and digital channels.

title: One in Three Workers Say Parents Face Greater Barriers to Career Progression
summary:
More than a third (34%) of workers believe working parents face greater challenges progressing in their careers, according to research from European financial technology provider payabl.
The figure rises to 43% among workers aged 18–34, compared with 21% of those aged 55 and over.
The research also highlights differences in perceptions of access to opportunities that can influence progression. Just 35% of women believe men and women receive equal networking opportunities at work, compared with 53% of men.
Almost three in ten women (29%) say childcare responsibilities can limit their ability to network or socialise with colleagues outside working hours. Among workers aged 18–34, this rises to 38%.
Jolita Strasunskaite, Group Chief People Officer at payabl., said: “Supporting working parents needs to go beyond parental leave. An organisation doesn't stand still while someone is away. Teams change, projects move forward and new opportunities emerge. Someone can return on the same salary and into the same role but still feel they have lost confidence, visibility or career momentum.
“Careers aren't built solely through formal promotion processes. Relationships and access to opportunities matter too. Employers need to understand whether their working practices create barriers for people with caring responsibilities.”
payabl. has introduced a dedicated Mum Support Group Programme to support employees through pregnancy, maternity leave, postpartum recovery and their transition back into work.
 
The four-month programme brings together small, confidential groups for specialist-led sessions covering emotional wellbeing, physical recovery, relationships, confidence, parenting and work-life integration. It is open to expectant mothers, employees on maternity leave, those returning to work and mothers of young children.
 
The programme aims to help employees navigate the transition into motherhood while maintaining confidence in their professional lives.
 
The initiative also supports the broader objectives of the EU Pay Transparency Directive, which aims to strengthen equal pay and address gender-based pay inequalities. By helping mothers maintain career momentum and access to professional opportunities, payabl. is taking practical steps to address some of the underlying factors that contribute to the gender pay gap.
 
Strasunskaite added: “A good maternity policy protects someone's employment. Supporting career continuity means thinking about what happens before they leave, while they're away and when they come back.
 
“Employers can't remove every challenge associated with parenthood, but we can make sure work isn't creating additional barriers. Having a child shouldn't unnecessarily mean choosing between being present for your family and continuing to build your career.”

Iress Unveils New AI-Enabled Capabilities in Xplan to Help Advisers Deliver Advice More Efficiently
summary:
Financial technology company Iress has unveiled the latest developments from its ongoing investment in its Xplan wealth management platform, with a series of enhancements designed to transform the advice experience. Combining an improved user experience, smarter workflows and new AI-enabled capabilities, the advances will help financial advisers reduce friction, improve client engagement and deliver advice more efficiently.
The announcement marks further progress in Iress’ product evolution strategy, which is focused on accelerating the development of its core platforms, modernising technology, embedding intelligence into existing workflows and delivering measurable productivity improvements for customers.
New Xplan AI-enabled capabilities designed around the advice workflow
The first phase of development in Iress’ Xplan Evolution programme focuses on making the power of Xplan easier to access, building on the advice data, workflows, modelling and compliance foundations that advice businesses already rely on.
Capabilities launched, or commencing rollout, include:
Xplan HQ: a new adviser workspace that brings together tasks, events, client opportunities and next best actions so advisers can prioritise work from a single, action-oriented view.
Xplan Porter AI: a new natural-language assistant that finds relevant information across Xplan without navigating multiple screens, making client data easier to find and use within the adviser workflow.
Xplan Meeting Assist AI: a new AI-enabled meeting assistant that supports meeting preparation and follow-up with summaries, suggested talking points and identified actions for adviser review.
Client Portal improvements: including refreshed user experience, smoother and more secure login and a new fact-find experience designed to make it easier for clients to provide information and collaborate with their adviser.
The new capabilities are being introduced progressively this year, with early user testing and staged rollout supporting a measured approach focused on reliability, security, and adviser control.
Iress UK CEO, Alistair Morgan, said: "Financial advisers need technology that makes the advice process simpler, more connected and more efficient. What’s important about Xplan Evolution is that we are embedding intelligence directly into the workflows advisers already trust and rely on, giving them a seamless experience.
"By making information easier to access and helping advisers identify what needs to happen next, we can make a meaningful difference to how advice is delivered and free up more time for clients.
“Just as importantly, these capabilities build on foundations that advice firms already trust, with security, reliability, permissions, and auditability fundamental to everything we develop. AI has enormous potential to improve productivity in financial advice, but its real value will depend on how effectively it is integrated into the advice journey, while keeping advisers firmly in control."
Iress Group CEO and Managing Director, Andrew Russell, said: "Over the past year, we've been focused on building a stronger, more competitive Iress. We're accelerating the evolution of our products, modernising the user experience and embedding AI directly into the workflows our customers rely on every day.
“Our ambition is straightforward: make financial advice more productive and our customers' businesses more competitive.
“Great specialist financial services software is difficult to build. It requires deep industry expertise, trusted data, sophisticated workflows and the reliability that comes from years of investment. These are significant strengths for Iress, and we're building on them.
“This is not about adding AI for the sake of it. It's about delivering better products that make a measurable difference to our customers. We know trust is earned through delivery, not promises. That's why we're focused on getting these capabilities into customers' hands, listening to their feedback and improving at pace.”
Xplan Evolution is part of Iress' ongoing programme of client-led product development. New capabilities are being shaped through customer research, beta programmes, product testing and roadmap conversations across the United Kingdom, Australia, South Africa and Canada.

The rollout forms part of Iress's broader product evolution strategy.
